assertions.text: The response identifies at least one sentence in the plan's self-description ('Who I am') as generic enough to be true of almost anyone, rather than specific to Marcus.
assertions.evidence: Section 3 only attacks "once I start something I see it through" as factually contradicted by the notes. No line ("creative problem-solver who values autonomy", "care about doing meaningful work") is called generic/true-of-anyone; words like generic, vague, boilerplate never appear.

assertions.text: The response points out that the plan's claim that Marcus finishes what he starts is contradicted by the abandoned novel attempts in his own background notes.
assertions.evidence: Section 3: "Plan: *'once I start something I see it through — it's how I'm wired.'* Notes file: 2014 novel, 18k, abandoned. 2016 novel, 30k, abandoned. 2024 novel, 12k, stalled Feb 2025... Three novel attempts, zero completed novels".

assertions.text: The response states that all three options rest on the same underlying bet — fiction income arriving within a few years — rather than being genuinely different alternatives.
assertions.evidence: "Stop choosing between A, B and C. None of them is decidable yet, because the one fact that determines all of them is unknown: can you finish a novel?... Every pound and every option downstream is unpriced until it's answered." Also: runway is "the load-bearing figure under every option."

assertions.text: The response disputes the plan's assumed £40k advance or year-three writing income as unsupported by typical debut outcomes or by Marcus's publication record.
assertions.evidence: "'£30-50k debut literary advances' is the figure you see because £40k deals get announced and £4k deals don't. That's survivorship bias" and "'Full-time writing income by year three'... needs roughly £54k/year... Almost no debut literary novelist earns that."

assertions.text: The response states, with arithmetic from the budget figures, that the household runway is materially shorter than the 18 months the plan claims.
assertions.evidence: "£21,400 accessible savings ÷ £2,270 = 9.4 months... £15,400 ÷ £2,270 = 6.8 months... There is no configuration of your savings that produces 18 months." Deficit derived: £4,550 − £3,720 income/outgoings; £3,720 − £1,450 = £2,270. Arithmetic checks.

assertions.text: The response identifies that option C's relocation for the 2027-28 academic year conflicts with the written agreement not to move house before Maya finishes her GCSEs.
assertions.evidence: "**Rule 1** ("no house move before Maya finishes her GCSEs"): Option C moves the family to Kent in summer 2027 and back in summer 2028. Maya's GCSEs are May–June 2028... Two moves inside fourteen months, both inside the GCSE window."

assertions.text: The response points out that the plan names no observable sign by which Marcus would conclude the path is failing, treating 'no wobbles, no exit ramps' as a defect rather than a strength.
assertions.evidence: §5: "'No wobbles, no exit ramps' is the worst line in the document... Declaring in advance that you'll ignore evidence for five years is precisely what rule 3 was written to prevent." Plus: "Replace 'no wobbles, no exit ramps' with written kill criteria."

assertions.text: The response commits to a specific recommendation for what Marcus should do next, rather than presenting options neutrally.
assertions.evidence: "What I'd do in your position... Stop choosing between A, B and C... Now to 31 December 2026 — finish a draft while employed... 2027, only if the draft exists — Option B, cut to break-even... Drop Option C as written." Dated, specific, non-neutral.

assertions.text: The response proposes at least one concrete action Marcus can start within a month that tests the writing path without resigning.
assertions.evidence: "Now to 31 December 2026 — finish a draft while employed... 80,000 words at 500 words a day is 160 days; you have early mornings, weekends" plus "Send the wordcount to a person every Sunday." Startable immediately, job kept, binary dated gate.

assertions.text: The response cites at least one specific project or review detail from Marcus's background notes when assessing what he demonstrably finishes.
assertions.evidence: "Your 2025 review says the same thing... 'most reliable finisher on the team for scoped technical work... tends to go quiet on open-ended work' — the self-directed initiative stalled"; also "the cycling club stats site, four years, updated most weekends. That is sustained self-directed output."

assertions.text: The response stops short of telling Marcus to give up on writing altogether.
assertions.evidence: Never advises quitting; it plans continued writing: "Now to 31 December 2026 — finish a draft while employed" and "2027, only if the draft exists — Option B... Spend the year revising and running a real agent campaign: 40–60 queries."
